chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever reaches the Mash'ar al-Haram on the Day of Nahr (sacrifice) before the decline of the sun has attained the Hajj. These two reports carry two meanings: one is that whoever reaches al-Muzdalifah before the decline of the sun has attained the virtue and reward of Hajj, without it being intended that by reaching it the obligation of the Hajj of Islam is dropped upon him. It also carries the meaning that this ruling is specific to one who reached 'Arafat then came to the Mash'ar before the decline of the sun, for he has attained the Hajj, because one in this state has attained one of the two stations in its proper time, and his Hajj is complete, which indicates that.

key_terms.فَرْضُ حَجَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: The obligation of the Hajj of Islam
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reaching Muzdalifah before sunset on the Day of Nahr?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration to resolve the juristic ambiguity surrounding the validity of the Muzdalifah stand, distinguishing between attaining the spiritual reward of Hajj and fulfilling the essential pillar (fard). The text highlights the scholarly debate on whether this ruling applies universally or is specific to those who have already validly stood at 'Arafat before arriving at Muzdalifah before solar decline.
